_doc: THE ONE DECLARATION of cloud-code's bottom navigation (#562). tabs.js builds the bar from this list in this order and nothing else restates it: the tester (test/test-cloud-nav.sh) renders the bar through the same tabs.js and reads the order back off the rendered model. `view` selects the renderer in index.js::VIEWS; `icon` is a class of Acode's own icon font (src/res/icons/style.css) and the tester proves each one exists there. The Editor tab is Acode itself (AI, the agent chat, replaced Home and is the default tab: every Home tile was a duplicate of a tab, and its Configs card moved to the top-right Profile & Config page), untouched: selecting it hides every cloud panel and nothing else.

nav._doc: Measured fit (#562): seven tabs is more than any fleet nav. At 360 px CSS width (the narrowest phone the owner's fleet targets) a tab is 51.4 px wide, above the 48 px touch floor, but 'MyTerminal' at 10 px is wider than its tab. So the bar does not truncate: tabs.js::fitLabels measures every label against its own tab on the device, and if ANY label overflows the bar switches to compact mode (icons for all tabs, the label only under the active one). min_viewport_px is the width the tester holds the touch floor to.

shared_store._doc: #575 -> cloud-shared-store: the store's declaration (storage.shared_root, storage.git_subdir) belongs to its owner, cloud-terminal-termux (ac_cloud-termux/build.json). NOTE: shared_root is now the LEGACY mirror folder on shared storage; this Cordova app still reads clones there until it moves onto the store provider. `app` is that fleet application id (build.json::name), never a path: tools/resolve-targets.py reads the sibling app's declaration at build time and writes the root AND its git folder (storage.git_subdir, #606/#676 — the ONE place the store keeps clones) into src/cloud/targets.gen.json, and index.js composes every on-device git-tree path as <cordova externalRootDirectory>/<root>/<git_subdir>/<relative>. No device-absolute path is written here — the user id in it changes under a second profile — and this app clones NOTHING: the Backlog reads and writes the clone cloud-drive's git manager keeps there.

backlog._doc: Backlog reads the ONE existing source: the dist output of cloud-me-pvt-tasks/1___BACKLOG___/1.1.Product-Backlog (built by its own build.js). Nothing here re-derives it: `entry` is loaded and rendered as-is, and every other view is reached through the links that file itself carries ('Views: per project · per status …'). That repository is PRIVATE and this APK is PUBLIC, so the backlog is never baked into the bundle; it is read on the device from the clone cloud-drive keeps in the shared store (#575): source_dir is RELATIVE to the store's git folder (shared_root/git_subdir, #676). The tab lets the owner point it elsewhere (kept in localStorage), and its edit / folder actions open the same files in Acode's editor, so a change is written back into that clone for cloud-drive to commit and push.
backlog._doc_index: #1699 the Backlog page opens on the clone's ROOT index.html (the whole rendered backlog, built by cloud-me-pvt-tasks' own CI), shown in a sandboxed frame with a Refresh action, a last-good copy kept in the app's data directory for offline use, and a visible reason when the clone cannot be read. Every earlier view stays: the 'Views' switch shows the dist/*.md pages (entry above, sub-pages, links, edit, repository, folder) exactly as before. `index` is RELATIVE to the repo root (nav.docs.root); `last_good` is a file in cordova.file.dataDirectory.

docs._doc: #1589 the Backlog tab's LEFT collapsible child file tree: the on-device clone of cloud-me-pvt-tasks (the Product-Backlog repo cloud-drive keeps in the shared store, #575/#676). `root` is RELATIVE to the store's git folder (shared_root/git_subdir), so no device-absolute path is written here; index.js composes it with gitPath(). It is a secondary tree (components/fileTree), not Acode's sidebar: a .md or .html opens RENDERED in place through the shared markdown/html preview (pages/markdownPreview). The folder is overridable per device (kept in localStorage docs.dir) for when the clone lives elsewhere.
docs.label: cloud-me-pvt-tasks

agents._doc: The Agents tab reads the SAME source as Backlog (#562: 'they must read ONE source'): the backlog engine already derives task-effort, task-complexity and agent-model per task and curates agent-slot from assignments.json, and emits them as its own views — 'agent batches' (entry, below) and 'per agent-model', which the entry links to in its Views line. This tab renders `entry` through the very renderer Backlog uses, from backlog.source_dir; nothing about agents is derived here. SEAM: seams.js::listAgents is where the LIVE half (running status, token utilisation from the agent runner) plugs in; until then the tab shows its note under the view.

repos._doc: On-device directory whose children are listed as repositories (a child holding .git): the shared store's git folder itself (#575/#676: shared_root/git_subdir, where cloud-drive actually clones), so what cloud-drive cloned is what Repos lists. `root` is RELATIVE to that git folder ('' = the folder itself). SEAM: seams.js::listRepos is the stub a real provider (gitea / cloud-myterminal's workspace broker) replaces.
repos._doc_volumes: The Git tab (was Repos) shows TWO volumes side by side, each a column headed by its name with the repos found in it listed below (a repo = an immediate subdirectory holding .git). `shared`: Cloud-Shared-Store/Git = the fleet store's git folder: tried at the store's real home (cld.termux private home, readable only under the shared uid) and, when that is unreadable, at the legacy shared-storage mirror (<shared storage>/<shared_root>/<git_subdir>) where cloud-drive still clones for this app. `emulated`: Emulated/Git = the Git folder of the primary emulated volume (storage/emulated/0), reached through cordova.file.externalRootDirectory (the primary emulated volume). Each folder is created when missing and both need all-files access (routed through Perms).

browser._doc: The Browser tab opens LOCAL pages in Acode's own in-app browser plugin (src/plugins/browser, the one Acode's Run command uses). `presets` are local servers the owner runs on the phone.

chat._doc: THE ONE DECLARATION of the Chat tab (replaced Home). The page is Cloud Search's chat (Chat > Search) without the search boxes: one message list, streamed replies, one composer. Everything fleet-shaped is DERIVED at build time by tools/resolve-targets.py into src/cloud/targets.gen.json: the agents (fleet_services, every service named agent_prefix*), the gateway URL (gateway.service's private_dns) and the fleet MCP servers (fleet_mcp, names only). What is declared here is only what the fleet data cannot say: the order the owner asked for (Hermes, OpenClaw first; 'cloud-code will use all agents possible'), what each backend accepts per request (model, effort, permission mode, MCP, functions), and the words.
chat._doc_fleet_services: The fleet's private service list as this repository carries it (cloud-c3 bakes it too). An agent is a service whose name starts with agent_prefix; its private_dns is where the mesh reaches it.
chat._doc_shared_agents: THE ONE agent descriptor list (libs:model-catalogue assets/agents/agents.json), read by Cloud Search's Agent field too. An agent's identity — label, X-Agent-Mode, health_key, fleet service, model kind/providers/default — comes from there (tools/resolve-targets.py merges it at build time into targets.gen.json chat.agent_decls); the entries below keep only the picker order and what is Cloud Code's own (effort, permission mode, MCP source, the claude CLI id map). An agent only in this file (OpenRouter · fleet) is Cloud Code's alone. The live gateway (/health.modes) stays the runtime check.
chat._doc_fleet_mcp: The derived .mcp.json (cloud-infra 1_cloud-configs/dist/mcp.json via _dotfiles/apps): the fallback MCP list for an agent whose backend publishes none. Only the server NAMES are copied; urls and headers stay out of the APK.
chat._doc_ai: THE SHARED AI CONTRACT (libs:ai assets/ai/ai.json), the file Cloud Search, Cloud Browser, Cloud Drive and Cloud Tools Small LLMs read through libs:ai. The gateway (my-ai-api on cloud-agi-goose, WireGuard-only: the OpenAI-style /v1/chat/completions that picks the agent with the X-Agent-Mode header, its /health, MCP, tools, sessions and models routes) and OpenRouter itself (the direct backend: url, models_url) are declared THERE and nowhere else: tools/resolve-targets.py copies them into targets.gen.json chat.ai, which the page merges over this block (chat.gateway, chat.direct). Cloud Code's `OpenRouter` backend takes the token from Profile & Config (or the fleet Account's); it is not an agent, just a plain streamed chat with the model picked in the catalogue.

model._doc: the gateway answers hermes mode with ITS model (/health.modes[hermes].model: the Hermes Agent's own once native, else HERMES_MODEL); a model in the request is ignored, so the button shows that model and does not pick

effort._doc: Behind the gateway's MCP loop (HERMES_API_KEY not wired) the gateway spreads every extra body field into its OpenRouter call, so reasoning.effort reaches the model when that model reasons. Once the gateway reaches the Hermes Agent's own API (/health.modes[hermes].native) it forwards only the messages: the agent runs its own reasoning settings, so the control is hidden then (unless_native).

permission._doc: Hermes' own approvals.mode is a container setting (off = auto); the gateway takes no per-request switch, so the mode is applied as the instruction below

mcp._doc: the gateway's live MCP list; Hermes' native API runs the same fleet MCP servers (its config.yaml mcp_servers is generated from the fleet mcp.json)

agents._doc: Nous Hermes Agent (cloud-agi-hermes). Its own API server is ON, loopback-only (127.0.0.1:8642, declared in the hermes compose since 2026-10-10), and the gateway's hermes mode reaches the REAL agent there once the gateway holds its key (HERMES_API_KEY, an owner sops edit). Until then the hermes mode is the Hermes model behind the gateway's MCP loop, and /health.modes[hermes].native says false: the picker shows which (agentSub). With the native API the More sheet gains Hermes' own skills, toolsets, sessions and scheduled jobs, live from the gateway.

model._doc: OpenClaw runs the model its own config names (cloud-u-containers user-ai_openclaw build.json runtime.model, through the gateway's OpenRouter face); the request's model field is the AGENT target (openclaw/default), so the button shows /health.modes[openclaw].model and does not pick

permission._doc: OpenClaw's HTTP API takes no per-request approval switch; applied as the instruction below

mcp._doc: no MCP server is configured in the fleet's OpenClaw (its tools are its own plugins), so the MCP sheet says so instead of listing servers it cannot call

agents._doc: OpenClaw (MIT, github.com/openclaw/openclaw), deployed 2026-10-10 as cloud-agi-openclaw on oci-apps: upstream's image, gateway on 127.0.0.1:18789 only, reached through the fleet gateway's openclaw mode (X-Agent-Mode: openclaw). Its catalogue row arrives with the next services_private.json regeneration; until then the live gateway's /health.modes is what says it is deployed. More gains its agent targets, live.
agents._doc_effort: null: the gateway forwards only the messages to OpenClaw (callNative); OpenClaw sets thinking in its own config

permission._doc: goose runs with no approval prompts in the gateway (operator, 2026-09-19)

agents._doc: Block's goose, the gateway's default agent (my-ai wraps goose).

model._doc: claude-superset-api runs the subscription claude CLI: an Anthropic row of the catalogue is passed as the CLI id (anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 -> claude-opus-5-5); other providers cannot be picked

permission._doc: the CLI has --permission-mode, but claude-superset-api takes no per-request flag; applied as the instruction below

agents._doc: The claude CLI on the subscription (cloud-agi-claude), through the gateway's claude-cli mode.

model._doc: the gateway's deepseek mode runs the requested deepseek/… model (v4-pro, v4-flash, v3.2, r1) and refuses any other (falls back to its DEEPSEEK_MODEL), so only the catalogue's DeepSeek rows can be picked

agents._doc: The DeepSeek harness (owner request): the fleet runs no DeepSeek agent of its own, so it is the gateway's deepseek mode — DeepSeek's models on OpenRouter inside the gateway's MCP tool loop, like goose and hermes. fleet null: it lives in the gateway; its live descriptor is /health.modes[deepseek] (shared with Cloud Search), and until the gateway serves it the picker says so.

agents.label: OpenRouter · fleet

model._doc: any catalogue row: the gateway's openrouter mode sends the requested model to OpenRouter (X-Agent-Mode: openrouter keeps a claude-… id off the claude CLI)

agents._doc: The fleet gateway's own OpenAI-compatible face (my-ai-api's openrouter mode): any model, streamed, paid by the gateway's key — no token on the phone. Not an agent with tools (no permission mode, no MCP), but the fleet's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it is in the picker. fleet null: it is deployed with the gateway itself.

chat._doc_agents: Listed first, in this order (the owner's: Hermes, OpenClaw, then the rest, then the gateway's own OpenRouter face). Then every mode the LIVE gateway lists in /health.modes that is not declared here (a new agent the gateway starts serving: generic controls, its model and functions from the gateway), then every OTHER fleet service named agent_prefix* that no mode reaches ('no app API yet', disabled). The direct OpenRouter backend comes last. States: ready, offline (the gateway did not answer: still selectable), unavailable (the gateway says so, with its reason), not deployed, no app API (model.js::resolveAgents).

permission._doc: The Permission Modes (ask, auto-edit, read-only, plan) and their default are the shared design's (ai-design.json permission), merged over this block by view.js and the tester. via=prompt per agent is declared in each agent's own `permission`.

catalogue._doc: The Model page is libs:model-catalogue (Cloud Search's catalogue, one implementation), narrowed by the lib's own filter to the four Text sections — A0 Code, A1 Agentic, A2 Base, A3 Reasoning — the same tables Cloud Search's chat model page shows. Drawn in HTML (this WebView app has no Compose) as a full page: one radio per row, exactly one selected, saved per agent (model.js::setAgentModel); rows the agent cannot run are greyed with the reason (model.js::rowState).

functions._doc: GET /sessions: the cross-device sessions (claude, goose); tap resumes one's tail into a new chat

functions.label: Search tools
functions._doc: GET /v1/mcp/search?q=: the MCP tools the agent can call

functions.label: Skills
functions.prompt: List the skills and toolsets you can use right now, one line each.
functions._doc: the prompt fallback while Hermes is behind the MCP loop; hidden once the gateway publishes Hermes' real /v1/skills (live:skills)

functions.label: Memory
functions.prompt: What do you remember about me and my current work? Read your memory first.

functions.label: Log Claude in (OAuth)
functions._doc: POST /auth/login/start on claude-superset-api returns the OAuth link; the code goes back to /auth/login/code

chat._doc_functions: The More sheet. 'gateway' = every agent served through the gateway. A toggle/select is shown only when the gateway's live /health.plugins lists its plugin (fetched each time the sheet opens); offline, the whole list falls back to this declaration, marked offline. kind: sessions/tools/info call the gateway route; toggle/select set a per-request header, persisted per agent; prompt sends the text as a message; login runs the Claude OAuth; client acts on the chat itself.

account._doc: Profile & Config > Account opens this fleet app (resolved like MyTerminal) and reads its OpenRouter key over libs:text-tools.

chat._doc_shared_catalogue: THE SHARED CATALOGUES (libs:ai assets/ai/ai-catalogue.json): the Model Catalogue's subpages (Frontier, Core, Specialist, Medium, Small) and the Task Catalogue (Big LLMs; Medium & Small LLMs). The resolver copies it into targets.gen.json chat.catalogue; the Model button's page and the Task button's page are drawn from it, Core being the model-catalogue tables below.
chat._doc_design: THE SHARED AI DESIGN (libs:ai assets/ai/ai-design.json): sizes, composer controls and their order, Permission Modes, Effort levels with `auto`, the More sheet's groups. tools/resolve-targets.py copies it into targets.gen.json chat.design (and the task mapping, ai-tasks.json, into chat.tasks); view.js sets every design metric as a --ai-* CSS custom property and draws the bar in the design's order. The Compose chat reads the same file, so the two cannot drift. Nothing about the look or the composer is restated in this file except which controls THIS app enables.

composer._doc: Which of the shared config bar's controls Cloud Code enables (ai-design.json defines them and their order: (+), Task, Agent, Model, Effort, Perms, MCP, (More)). Effort and Perms still appear only where the chosen agent takes them. default_task: the task the first chat opens on (empty = none); task_required false: the user can clear it.

chat._doc_effort: Effort levels (Auto, Low, Medium, High, Max) are the shared design's (ai-design.json effort), sent as OpenRouter's reasoning.effort; Auto sends nothing.

myterminal._doc: THE ONE PLACE the MyTerminal target is named (#562). It is a fleet application id, never a package: tools/resolve-targets.py reads the sibling app whose build.json::name equals it and derives the package (android.application_id) and the launcher activity (its manifest) into src/cloud/targets.gen.json at build time. #561 renamed cloud-ide to cloud-myterminal; if a later rename happens, this one value moves and the resolver fails the build loudly until it does.

_doc_pages: #1158 SECOND ROW. tabs[].pages are the sub-pages of a bottom page, drawn by bars-dom.js as the shared second row (libs:ui-nav-bars) when a tab has two or more. Cloud Code's only sub-pages are the views the backlog engine already emits as dist files (P-Backlog-<id>.md): Backlog = status, project, priority, effort; Agents = batches, models. The first page's file is the tab's own nav.<tab>.entry. `icon` is a class of Acode's icon font (the tester proves each exists).

superapp._doc: #1158 the first row's AI icon hands over to the SuperApp, whose assistant it is (extapp:cloud-superapp/ai, as every app without an assistant of its own does). A fleet application id, resolved by tools/resolve-targets.py like MyTerminal and Cloud Account (Profile = chat.account.app).

bars._doc: #1158 THE SHARED DESIGN OF #1154 AS DATA. This app is a Cordova WebView with no Compose (see index.js), so the shared Compose libs cannot draw its bars; bars-dom.js draws the same bars from these numbers (dp = CSS px) and colours (Kotlin ARGB literals, 0xAARRGGBB). Every value equals the lib constant it is named for and the nav-shape guard (rule W) reads the Kotlin and fails on drift: first_row = libs:ui-nav-bars TopFirstRowSpec, second_row = libs:ui-nav-bars SecondRowSpec, bottom = libs:ui-nav-bars BottomSpec (+ libs:bottomnav SearchHtmlTokens), theme = libs:theme-background ThemeBackground. Change the lib, then this file, never this file alone. At rest every bottom item and every second-row tab shows its name; scrolled down only the selected one does (#1159). A bottom label that would not fit its cell is never truncated: the bar then names the selected item only (tabs.js::fitLabels, #565).

collapse._doc: Scroll down past threshold_px hides the first row and compacts the second row (tabs of second_row.compact_tab_height, only the selected one keeps its name) and the bottom bar (bottom.collapsed_height, only the selected item keeps its label); scroll up (or the top of the list) restores all three (libs:bottomnav NavChromeScroll, #1157/#1159). Scrolls within settle_ms of a change are ignored, so the resize of the page cannot read as a scroll back. threshold_px and settle_ms are this app's: the lib's rule is its own scroll connection.
